newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND BARCELONA PREPARE FOR MARATHON MONTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND BARCELONA PREPARE FOR MARATHON MONTH.

text.p: Atletico Madrid and Barcelona are set for a marathon month in which quarter-final cup ties at home and in Europe mean they will each play four games more than league leaders Real Madrid.

With 10 games in a make-or-break 35 days in which they will never go more than four days without a match, the two sides may pay the price of a nationwide decision to give players a Christmas break by rescheduling fixtures from the end of December.
In the same period there will only be eight days in which no game is played, and Spanish fans will be able to watch at least one live televised match on each of more than 20 nights.
The eyes of Barcelona fans will be on beleaguered coach Bobby Robson.

The former England manager must have thought he had earned some breathing space by knocking arch-rivals Real Madrid out of the Spanish Cup. But then Barcelona drew Atletico in the quarter-finals and were hit by a series of bad results.
And Robson had to take the blame for giving Ronaldo a holiday when Spanish papers carried photographs of the Brazilian striker dancing the samba in the Rio carnival.
Robson will again be in the firing line if Barcelona come home from fifth-placed Real Sociedad on Thursday with anything less than a win.
League games with Zaragoza, Tenerife, Compostela, Logrones and Sevilla follow, together with a Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final against Sweden's AIK Stockholm.
The Cup competitions may yet offer Robson a life-line. Or they could sink him.
Next month Barcelona travel to Atletico for the first leg of their Spanish Cup quarter-final.
Atletico-Barcelona games are traditionally dramatic, high-scoring, and above all exhausting affairs.
Robson brought in some new faces for Sunday's 1-0 win over Racing Santander, and may be forced to call upon all the reserves of one of Europe's strongest squads to confront the marathon schedule.

Atletico survived last year's league and cup double campaign using a hard-core of just 13 players. Coach Radomir Antic has tried to repeat the trick but is likely to feel the lack of depth in his squad in the coming month.
Unlike last season, Antic's men are involved in continental competition, and have found mighty Ajax Amsterdam blocking their way to the European Cup semi-finals.
Antic may rest his top players ahead of the Ajax games if he feels the championship is no longer a viable prospect now the gap with neighbours Real has grown to an alarming 16 points.
Ironically Real Madrid's disastrous 1995-96 season may have set up the club for their 1996-97 campaign.

The six-times European champions failed to qualify for continental competition for only the second time in their history. Not only are they out of Europe, but early Spanish Cup elimination has left Real to concentrate on winning a record 27th title.
Finding spare days to play postponed games has become no easy matter since the summer of 1995 when the league was increased to 22 teams.

Last year the league was played in nine rather than ten months because of the Euro 96 tournament, and this season the need to allow the national side time to prepare for World Cup qualifying matches has meant there have been some weekends without club football.
First division clubs only played three games in December because of a match between Spain and Yugoslavia and the decision to give players a seasonal break.
But in place of the lost weekends, Spanish fans have found themselves in the unfamiliar position of watching midweek league action.
And Barcelona and Atletico -- two of the clubs most strongly opposed to the change of dates -- may be the ones to suffer.
